outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: (a) the gate_red_lines docstring now says a gate run inside `next` that repeated a red opens with the banner, and that a background red is read off its row by recorded_red with no banner. (b) The module docstring now says the background row is read back by read_back. A red is acted on as the row records it. A green is asked again, which repeats each step that grades the tree while nothing it graded has moved, and measures an entry naming a path its identity leaves out. A comment in run_followers had the same fault and is fixed: it said a background red reaches it as a repeat. (c) New SIGNAL_STEP_BYTES, SIGNAL_FORMS_KEY, signal_step_name and say_clause. step_seconds takes a name speller. repeat_said returns (clause, signal form); read_back records both. signal_line carries a clause's signal form when one is recorded. Each name in the signal form goes through _flat, has `; ` replaced, and past the width is cut to head...tail. The plain did-line and --explain keep every name whole. Measured: with names unclipped, the clause's fixed text alone (with the run id) is longer than the room fit_rest leaves on the sign-off step. So clipping alone could not keep the clause on the line, and the signal form also drops the run id and the repeated names; it keeps a count of the repeated steps. (d) Decision: leave the stage out. _task_timing.stage_problems requires an ISO startedAt, a repeat row records none, and the module rule is that a missing source is named, never read as zero. row_stages now answers a verdictSource=reused row with `evidence row <R> repeated the verdict of run <S> rather than measuring it, and records no start of its own`. Comments I read that speak of reading a gate back, repeating a verdict or measuring again, found by what they say. Changed: module docstring, gate_red_lines, run_followers comment, row_stages, repeat_said, read_back, signal_line, step_seconds. Unchanged and still true: the set-aside paragraph of the module docstring; the gate-red-base-unknown options comment; GATE_REUSED_BANNER comment; ledger_unread; the reviewer-redispatch docstring; gate_row; gate_row_read; verdict_taken; note_basis; the base-mark block comment; unmeasurable_bound; red_runs; base_reading_for and its bound comment; base_gate; the scope-run rerun docstring; record_gate; task_gate; follow_red_gate; the gate_step queue_row comment; the GATE_LAUNCH_KEY block comment; chosen_task_gate; unrepeatable_red; recorded_red; GATE_LEFT_OUT; repeat_reason; background_gate; the measure-base and redo answer comments; chosen_phase_gate. tests/test_drive_phase.py: helpers _rb_signal_back and _rb_pieces, and cases rd8, rd9 and rd10 in a new _readback_signal_cases, run by the rd-block. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the read-back paragraph describes the signal form, and the timing paragraph describes the repeat sentence. Commands, each exit 0: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py` -> `1/1 files ok, 1023 cases`; `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__deps.py` -> 284 cases ok; `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__output_lints.py` -> 183 cases ok; `ruff check` and `vermin -t=3.8-` on the two .py files. Mutations were made in memory: the source was compiled under its real path in a scratch probe, and the checkout was not written. No clip turns rd8 and rd9 red. No separator replacement turns rd9 red. Forms unread turns rd8 and rd9 red. No repeat branch turns rd10 red. Unmutated, all three pass. Not run: the --spaced sweep; the new cases build no command from a new path. Dependants: the signal line's field rules are unchanged, since the head, the ` | ` fields and the read-clause handling are untouched, and the sn blocks pass inside the full sweep. /audit:status prints recorded stages: no stage's shape changed, a repeat row built no stage before and builds none now, and only the did-line sentence differs. The other importers of drive-phase.py use none of the changed signatures: a grep for repeat_said and step_seconds over plugins, tests, tools and .claude/hooks finds only drive-phase.py. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's dependants are basename and prose references to the guide; no heading or file name changed.
